 Batters should have won this match for us: Taskin
 Published : 18 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 18 October 2026, 07:00
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Star Sports Desk 
 Photo: ACB 
 Pacer Taskin Ahmed admitted that a lack of game awareness and an inability to build partnerships led to Bangladesh’s heavy defeat against Zimbabwe in the opening match of the UAE ODI Tri-Series at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi yesterday. 
 Bangladesh suffered a 99-run defeat against Sikandar Raza-led Zimbabwe, who secured their first win under Raza’s ODI captaincy, as the Tigers were bundled out for 172 in 33.4 overs while chasing a target of 272.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 In a tri-series also involving Afghanistan, the defeat dealt a major blow to Bangladesh’s net run rate, which dropped to -1.980.
 Taskin was quick to identify where the Tigers went wrong.
 “270 (272) was definitely chaseable,” Taskin said at the post-match press conference.
 “We really didn't play well. I mean, we should have chased this. Unfortunately, we couldn't build a single partnership; just one partnership would have won us the game. In terms of batting, I think our batters should have won this match for us. But unfortunately, they couldn't. Still, there is one game left.”
 Bangladesh made flying starts with both the ball and the bat. After being sent in to bowl, Taskin struck three times early to reduce Zimbabwe to 24 for three in seven overs.
 However, Zimbabwe showed resilience as Brendan Taylor and Craig Ervine combined for a 150-run fourth-wicket partnership to help their side recover.
 “No matter if I get three or five wickets, it is of no use if we don't win the match,” Taskin added, highlighting the team’s shortcomings.
 Taylor (81 off 101 balls) and Ervine (93 off 106) both missed out on centuries, but their efforts, along with unbeaten 21-run knocks from tailenders Newman Nyamhuri and Wellington Masakadza, helped Zimbabwe post a challenging total.
 Bangladesh then made a promising start to their chase, thanks to an aggressive 46 off 38 balls from opener Tanzid Tamim. His innings, however, remained the highest individual score by a Bangladeshi batter in the match, as the Tigers failed to build a substantial partnership after he departed in the 10th over.
 “We had a great start, and it is also true that the pitch was quite good for batting. They actually showed that, regardless of being under pressure, building a partnership on a good pitch makes it possible for any team to achieve a decent score,” Taskin said.
 Unable to rotate the strike as dot balls piled up during the middle overs, several Bangladesh batters threw their wickets away with poor shot selection. Taskin stressed that the team needed to improve its awareness of match situations.
 “The problem lies in consistency; it's evident that we need to build this consistency and game awareness. We lack a bit more in game awareness. Because everyone has the skill, and anyone who watches cricket knows that every batsman has proven they can bat well. So sometimes you will see that team-wise, we collapse very quickly when under pressure.”
 Bangladesh will next face Afghanistan on October 21, after the Afghans take on Zimbabwe tomorrow at the same venue.
